baseline:
C
A cheetah's speed is not constant; it accelerates and decelerates. Understanding its speed at a specific instant provides a more accurate and detailed picture of its motion than an average speed would, which is true for many real-world processes where the rate of change varies.

D
The average rate of change over an interval is the change in the function's output (Δy) divided by the change in the input (Δx). Geometrically, this is the slope of the straight line (the secant line) that connects the two points on the graph corresponding to the ends of that interval.

B
The average rate of change describes the overall change across an interval, but it doesn't reveal the specific, instantaneous rate at any single moment within that interval.

B
The slope of the tangent line at a single point is the definition of the instantaneous rate of change of the function at that precise point, also known as the derivative.

B
Instantaneous speed is the value of the derivative of the position function at a specific time. The derivative of the position function s(t) = t² is the velocity function v(t) = 2t. At t = 2, the speed is v(2) = 2(2) = 4 units per time.
